name: GPU-Accelerated HPC Cluster on Microsoft Azure
tagline: Scalable AI training and HPC on Azure with GPU acceleration
description: A cloud-native platform that provisions GPU-accelerated HPC clusters on Microsoft Azure for large-scale AI model training and high-performance computing. Built on NVIDIA Hopper and Ada Lovelace GPUs with Azure ND H100 VMs and Azure Kubernetes Service, it delivers optimized compute, networking, and power solutions for modern workloads.
overview: The product enables rapid deployment and management of GPU clusters for AI training, HPC simulations, and mixed-precision workloads. Leveraging Azure’s managed compute, high-speed InfiniBand interconnects, and automated sizing, it ensures efficient resource utilization, low latency, and transparent cost visibility.
problem: Organizations struggle to design and operate GPU-enabled clusters without standardized methodologies, resulting in mis-sized instances, underutilization, costly power consumption, and complex networking challenges.
intelligence: Integrates AI-driven workload profiling, mixed-precision training support, and automated sizing algorithms to maximize throughput, memory efficiency, and training convergence.
modules: Hardware selection, Compute sizing engine, Power & cooling management, Networking architecture, Container orchestration, Monitoring suite, TCO analyzer
architecture: Composes of compute nodes running Azure ND H100 v5 VMs with NVLink, a non-blocking spine-leaf InfiniBand fabric providing GPUDirect RDMA, Azure Kubernetes Service for pod orchestration, centralized monitoring stack, and unified storage tiers.
technology: NVIDIA H100/H200 GPUs, NVIDIA Quantum-2 InfiniBand, Azure ND H100 v5 VMs, Azure Kubernetes Service, Cloud API gateways, Azure Monitor, Kubernetes CNI overlay
security: Enforces VM isolation, VNet segregation, private endpoints, RBAC for AKS, encrypted data at rest and in transit, regular patching, and compliance with data residency standards.
performance: Delivers up to 67 TFLOPS per H100 GPU, >4 TB/s memory bandwidth, multi-terabyte inter-node InfiniBand links, and scales to hundreds of nodes; power density supports up to 30–40 kW per rack; achieves >95% GPU utilization under optimal workloads.
testing: Validates sizing through corrected FLOP calculations, runs benchmarked training jobs (e.g., 175-B parameter models), performs stress tests on network fabrics, conducts power and cooling simulations, and employs chaos engineering to verify resilience.
roadmap: Planned enhancements include integration of upcoming Blackwell GPUs, expansion into quantum chemistry and genomics HPC, smarter auto-scaling for burst workloads, deeper energy-aware scheduling, and federated multi-cluster service discovery.
